Thanks — adding a few compliance-specific clarifications below that I’ll also add into the MAP spreadsheet under the Compliance row.

- Logging retention: Redwood can provide configurable retention per-log-type. We support exported audit-trail bundles in NDJSON/CSV for customer archival and can hold canonical logs for up to 7 years on dedicated plans (requires reserved capacity bucket). For hosted customers, we default to 180 days unless otherwise contracted.
- Evidence & audit artifacts: We can produce time-ordered audit bundles (requestable via API) containing request metadata, model version, token hashes (redacted), and KMS key IDs. We cannot provide raw token content for PHI unless under explicit contract and approved access controls; instead we offer redaction and hashed-record linking.
- PHI/PII scoping: We recommend a scoping worksheet (I’ve added a tab in the MAP) that enumerates fields, retention need, and processing rationale. If HealthLytics requires PHI processing, we will need a signed DPA + Business Associate Addendum (BAA) before any PHI sample ingestion.

I’ll add the minimum evidence types and sample API commands to extract audit bundles into the spreadsheet by 2026-11-05 as requested.

— Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Lauren / team — quick tech note on tenant separation and logging options:

- Option 1 (Logical separation): single audit stream with tenant_id field + per-tenant retention policies enforced by lifecycle tags. Lower operational cost, faster delivery.
- Option 2 (Physical separation): dedicated audit buckets per tenant (recommended for regulated PHI customers). Higher cost but simpler evidence separation for audits.

For HealthLytics, given the mix of regulated and non-regulated workflows you described, I suggest Option 2 for the regulated pipeline and Option 1 for ephemeral session logs. I’ll draft a small implementation runbook and an estimate for storage + retrieval overhead by 2026-11-09.

Also: we can script automated exports on a weekly cadence to an external S3 bucket you control (requires cross-account role). If HealthLytics wants weekly immutable snapshots for long-term retention, that will be part of the contract appendix (storage costs scoped separately).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
